content: 1. Studies conducted in rural community-based settings in India and China suggest that digital tracking of client information with clinical decision support likely increases the number of children under 5 years receiving the Polio 3 vaccine. The certainty of this evidence is moderate. 2. The same approach likely makes little or no difference in the number of children under 5 years receiving the DPT 3 vaccine. This conclusion is also based on studies conducted in rural community-based settings in India and China, with moderate certainty. 3. In China, a study with low certainty suggests that digital tracking with clinical decision support likely makes little or no difference in the number of children under 5 years receiving the Measles vaccine. 4. In the USA, a study with very low certainty indicates that the effect of this approach on emergency department visits among children with pulmonary disease is uncertain. 5. In India, a study with moderate certainty suggests that digital tracking with clinical decision support likely makes little or no difference in the number of women giving birth at a healthcare facility. 6. The same approach in India likely increases the number of pregnant women attending at least three antenatal care visits, with moderate certainty. 7. In India, the approach likely makes little or no difference in the number of pregnant women receiving at least two tetanus injections, based on moderate certainty evidence. 8. No studies were identified to assess the effect of this approach on the timeliness of receiving healthcare services. Therefore, the effect on the time between presentation and appropriate management is uncertain. 9. In India, the approach likely increases the number of pregnant women taking at least 90 iron tablets during pregnancy, with moderate certainty. 10. The approach likely increases the number of women initiating immediate breastfeeding in India, with moderate certainty. 11. In India, the approach likely makes little or no difference in the number of women exclusively breastfeeding for six months, based on moderate certainty evidence. 12. A study in India with low certainty suggests that the approach may make little or no difference in the number of women using contraception within six months after birth. 13. In India, the approach likely increases the number of women using contraception six months or later after giving birth, with moderate certainty. 14. No studies were identified to assess the effect of this approach on providers' or patients' satisfaction or acceptability. Therefore, the effect on these outcomes is uncertain. 15. No studies were identified to assess the effect of this approach on the quality of data about services provided. The effect on this outcome is uncertain. 16. The cost of implementing the digital intervention is estimated at $66 per patient for setup, $62 per patient annually for operating costs, and $53 every three years per healthcare provider for mobile phone replacement. These costs do not include management expenses. 17. A study in India with very low certainty suggests that the effect of this approach on resource use is uncertain. 18. In Bangladesh, studies with very low certainty indicate that the effect of this approach on the number of children fully immunized in rural or urban settings is uncertain. 19. In Bangladesh, a study with very low certainty suggests that the effect of this approach on the number of children receiving BCG and Pentavalent vaccines in rural settings is uncertain.
